description.value: Vancouver Lookout is a 168-metre observation tower atop Harbour Centre in downtown Vancouver, opened in 1977 and inaugurated by Neil Armstrong — at the time the tallest building in the city. A glass elevator whisks visitors to a 360° deck with views spanning Stanley Park, Gastown, the North Shore Mountains, and the working port. Centrally located across from Waterfront Station, it makes a natural landmark stop mid-ride for cyclists exploring the downtown core or Seawall.

bike_parking_detail: 7 racks within 100m: stands (9 spaces) at 47m; stands (2 spaces) at 54m; stands (4 spaces) at 62m; stands (2 spaces) at 63m; stands (4 spaces) at 75m; stands (2 spaces) at 80m; rack (2 spaces) at 82m. Total: 25 spaces.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms bike racks off Hastings Street (Plan Your Visit page), wheelchair-accessible washrooms on deck (FAQ and multiple subpages), and free Wi-Fi (FAQ). The FAQ explicitly states no food is available for purchase on deck. OSM hours differ substantially from the website's stated hours (OSM: 09:00–21:00 / 08:30–22:30 seasonal; website: 10 AM–6 PM daily), suggesting the OSM hours are outdated.
concerns: OSM opening_hours tag (Oct-May 09:00-21:00; Jun-Sep 08:30-22:30) conflicts significantly with the website's current stated hours (10 AM to 6 PM daily, last elevator 5:30 PM). OSM hours appear substantially outdated and should be corrected.
OSM name is 'Harbour Centre Lookout Tower' but the operator and website consistently use 'Vancouver Lookout' (also captured in alt_name tag). The alt_name may be the more recognisable public name.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, open, publicly accessible landmark attraction in downtown Vancouver. Bike racks on Hastings Street make it a practical stop for touring cyclists.
enrichment_extras.notes: The website lists an email address (info@vancouverlookout.com) not present in the OSM record; may be worth adding. No phone number was surfaced in the fetched website text, so phone confirmation is marked null.

Café or food on site.detail: Website FAQ: 'Is there food available for purchase on deck? No, visitors are welcome to bring outside food and non-alcoholic beverages.'

wow_evidence: 168m observation deck (1977, opened by Neil Armstrong), 360-degree views over the city, port, and mountains; paid elevator, day-enhancing. Misfiled as Park / Nature.
blurb: 360-degree observation deck 168 metres above downtown; glass elevator ride up.
